answers.why: Judah is the kingdom that would fall along with its king Amaziah.
Judah's forces are defeated and flee to their tents.
Israel is the opposing kingdom whose forces defeat Judah.
The gate of Ephraim names a geographical connection with Ephraim's tribal territory.
Azariah restores Elath to the kingdom of Judah.
Jeroboam son of Nebat led the nation of Israel into sin.
The LORD is called Israel's God in an account of restoring the nation's borders.
The LORD sees the bitter affliction of the Israelite population.
Israel is the afflicted nation with no helper.
The LORD preserves Israel's national existence and saves them through Jeroboam.
Judah denotes the kingdom associated with the former possession of Damascus and Hamath.
Israel is the kingdom for which Jeroboam recovers Damascus and Hamath.
